title: Half-degree shape classification under binary polynomial composition
statement: Let f and sigma be monic binary polynomials of positive degrees n and k, and suppose deg(f-x^n)<=floor(n/2). Then f(sigma) has no nonleading term above floor(nk/2) if and only if sigma=x^k, or n is a power of two and deg(sigma-x^k)<=floor(k/2).

evidence.supports: The arithmetic largest-proper-submask criterion, equivalent power-of-two classification, direct Horner composition, and independence from the shaped source tail.
evidence.notes: The universal step is the distinct-degree Frobenius expansion recorded in ADR-0566. The 868 map/degree and 5580 varied-source cells are mutation controls, not a replacement for that argument.

notes: This theorem classifies shape preservation only. Irreducibility of a permitted composition remains a separate certificate obligation.
